newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesia reduces July heavy sweet crude exports.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia reduces July heavy sweet crude exports.

text.p: Indonesia's export allocations of heavy sweet Minas and Duri crudes for July have been cut from June because of a rise in domestic demand, traders said.
But total allocations for July were unchanged from June at around 175-180,000 barrels per day (bpd).

The extra domestic requirements for Minas and Duri were for the 125,000 bpd Exor-1 refinery at Balongan, which Pertamina is planning to run at maximum capacity, to make up for a one-month maintenance shutdown at the 200,000-bpd crude unit at Balikpapan refinery. The shut down starts July 10.
Exor-1 refines mainly Minas and Duri crudes, but has enough upgrading facilities to produce a substantial volume of middle distillates.
Indonesian state-owned Pertamina reduced Minas July allocations by 10,000 bpd from June, while the Duri volumes were lower by 13,000 bpd month on month.
The planned shutdown of the Balikpapan refinery also led to an increase in the allocations of light sweet Belida crude.
Balikpapan refines a large volume of Belida.
